newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-INVENTIVE RHODES GIVES S. AFRICA RESPECTABILITY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INVENTIVE RHODES GIVES S. AFRICA RESPECTABILITY.

text.p: A typically inventive 83 not out from Jonty Rhodes helped South Africa to an unlikely 245 for eight against Australia on a slow and low pitch in the third one day international at Newlands on Wednesday.
South Africa were in deep trouble at 106 for five in the 29th over after stand-in Australian skipper Ian Healy -- deputising for Mark Taylor who was rested -- won the toss and chose to field.
A 70-run partnership between Rhodes and Natal team mate Derek Crookes (18) rescued the innings.

Rhodes' 11th one day half century -- he also has a century to his name -- came in only 52 balls and he even accelerated after that, hitting Shane Warne for a six and adding six fours in his 77-ball innings.

With Shaun Pollock blasting 21 in just 15 balls in a 40-run partnership in five overs with Rhodes and Rudi Bryson contributing 17 in seven balls as 23 came off the last 10 deliveries, South Africa completed a magnificent transformation.
Warne's last over went for 18 to leave him with figures of two for 64 in 10 overs.
Earlier, openers Louis Koen (22) Herschelle Gibbs (28) were beaten frequently by the new ball but managed to put on 52 before falling within a run of each other.
Daryll Cullinan (12) and Jacques Kallis (23) put on 27 before they and Hansie Cronje (three) all fell within the space of six overs to set the scene for Rhodes' heroics.
Australian opener Mark Waugh split webbing on his right hand in dropping a catch off Kallis at slip and is expected to bat only if required.
The seven-match series is level at one game apiece.
